newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's of London signs Polaris agreement.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's of London signs Polaris agreement.

text.p: Lloyd's of London said on Friday it had signed up to become a full member of Polaris, the insurance industry's electronic initiative for distribution of personal lines products to brokers.
Lloyd's will provide an "umbrella' arrangement, enabling smaller syndicates to participate in Polaris where individual syndicate membership may be deterred by cost.
John Stratton, managing director of Polaris UK Ltd welcomed the Lloyd's move, which he said represented "a milestone both for Polaris and for the industry".

"Many other insurers, brokers and software houses have been waiting for the Lloyd's announcement and this strong endorsement can only be good for the future expansion of Polaris usage," said Stratton.

Polaris has been introduced in response to intense competition in the personal lines market and since its inception in 1994 has attracted membership representing more than 85 percent of the UK personal lines motor market.
It is hoped Polaris will help strengthen Lloyd's syndicates existing links with high street brokers and allow participants to get product to the market more quickly and cheaply.
Lloyd's underwriters account for around 14 percent of the UK motor market and 12 leading Lloyd's motor syndicates have already signed up.
Polaris is working on extending its household and commercial lines capabilities.
